subject: Business
title: Platform vs. Product Businesses
description: A quick win: understand Platform vs. Product Businesses.

hook.text: Apple doesn't write most iPhone apps. It built a platform and let millions of developers do it.

buildup.text: A product business sells what it makes. A platform lets others build and sell on top of it.

discovery.text: Platforms scale exponentially because each new participant adds value without extra platform effort.

twist.text: Platforms must solve a cold start problem: no developers without users, no users without apps.

climax.text: Amazon went from selling books to hosting everyone's apps on AWS. Product to platform.

punchline.text: Products make things. Platforms make ecosystems.

quiz.question: What is the cold start problem for platforms?
options: Needing users and developers simultaneously before either exists
The high cost of initial server infrastructure

details.summary: Product businesses create and sell goods or services directly, while platform businesses create infrastructure for others to create and exchange value. Platforms like YouTube, iOS, and Shopify scale faster because participants generate value, but they require solving the cold start problem first.
details.whyItMatters: Platform businesses have produced the most valuable companies of the last two decades because they leverage other participants' resources to scale.
takeaways: Product businesses sell directly while platforms enable others to create and exchange value
Platforms scale faster because participants generate the value, not the platform owner
The cold start problem of attracting initial participants is the main platform challenge

faq.question: When should a startup choose a platform model over a product model?
faq.answer: When the market has clear two-sided dynamics with supply and demand that can be matched. When network effects can create defensive moats. When the value is best created by participants rather than the company. Product models are better when you control quality and direct customer experience.

faq.question: Can a company transition from product to platform?
faq.answer: Yes. Amazon started selling books then built a marketplace. Apple sold devices then built the App Store. Salesforce sold CRM then built an app platform. The product provides initial distribution and trust, which can be leveraged to attract platform participants later.
